title: The Monkey King's Sacrifice
summary: A monkey king uses his body as a bridge to save his troop from hunters, sacrificing himself.
moral: A true leader sacrifices for the welfare of others

acts.summary: Hunters corner the monkeys at a cliff

acts.name: sacrifice
acts.summary: Monkey king stretches his body as a bridge

acts.name: lesson
acts.summary: Hunter is moved and frees the troop

title: The Golden Deer
summary: A golden deer saves a drowning man who later betrays the deer's location to the king.
moral: Ingratitude is the worst of all vices

acts.name: betrayal
acts.summary: Man reveals deer's location for reward

acts.name: justice
acts.summary: King is shamed and protects the deer

title: The Wise Quail
summary: Quails escape a hunter's net by flying together, but infighting later causes their capture.
moral: Unity saves; quarreling destroys

acts.name: unity
acts.summary: Quails fly together and lift net

title: The Elephant and the Blind Men
summary: Six blind men each touch a different part of an elephant and argue about what it is.
moral: Partial knowledge leads to incomplete understanding

title: The Hare's Sacrifice
summary: A hare offers to sacrifice himself in fire for a hungry traveler, who is actually a god.
moral: The greatest gift is selfless sacrifice

acts.name: hunger
acts.summary: A traveler asks animals for food

acts.name: reward
acts.summary: God reveals himself and honors the hare

moral: Compassion can change even a hunter's heart

acts.name: pact
acts.summary: Deer send one daily for king's kitchen

acts.name: sacrifice
acts.summary: Deer king takes pregnant doe's place

acts.name: mercy
acts.summary: King is moved and bans all hunting

title: The Crow and the Owl
summary: Crows and owls are eternal enemies; a crow spy infiltrates the owls and burns their home.
moral: Beware of enemies posing as friends

acts.name: enmity
acts.summary: Crows and owls are at war

acts.name: infiltration
acts.summary: Clever crow pretends to be exiled

title: The Foolish Lion
summary: A lion befriends a jackal who flatters him; the jackal leads the lion into a trap.
moral: Flattery is the tool of deceivers

acts.name: trap
acts.summary: Jackal leads lion to hunter's pit

title: The Merchant and the Dead Mouse
summary: A poor boy starts with a dead mouse and trades his way up to wealth through cleverness.
moral: With cleverness and hard work, even nothing can become something

acts.name: trade
acts.summary: Through clever trades he builds wealth

title: The Tortoise and the Monkeys
summary: Monkeys bully a tortoise; the tortoise pretends to be dead and is thrown into a pond, escaping.
moral: Cleverness can overcome brute strength

title: The Jackal and the Crow
summary: A jackal tricks a crow into dropping its food by engaging it in conversation.
moral: Do not let flattery make you drop your guard

title: The King's White Elephant
summary: A captured white elephant refuses to eat until reunited with his blind mother.
moral: Devotion to parents is the noblest virtue

acts.name: grief
acts.summary: Elephant refuses to eat or drink

acts.name: reunion
acts.summary: King sends elephant home to blind mother

title: The Cunning Wolf
summary: A wolf pretends to be a vegetarian holy man; when prey comes close he pounces.
moral: Judge by actions, not by outward appearance

title: The Parrot and the Fig Tree
summary: A loyal parrot refuses to leave a dying fig tree; the gods reward its loyalty by reviving the tree.
moral: True loyalty is rewarded

acts.name: friendship
acts.summary: Parrot lives in a fig tree

title: The Crab and the Crane
summary: A crane eats fish by pretending to relocate them; a crab catches on and kills the crane.
moral: The deceiver meets justice from the unexpected

acts.name: trick
acts.summary: Crane offers to move fish to larger pond

acts.name: deception
acts.summary: Crane eats fish at a rock

title: The Mongoose and the Farmer's Wife
summary: A mongoose kills a snake to protect a baby but is killed by the farmer's wife who acts in haste.
moral: Never act in haste without knowing the truth

title: The Wise Goat
summary: A goat about to be sacrificed laughs and cries; explains he laughs at freedom and cries for the priest's karma.
moral: Every action has consequences

title: The Sandy Road
summary: A merchant caravan crosses a desert; they throw away water too early and nearly perish.
moral: Do not abandon what sustains you before reaching safety

acts.name: folly
acts.summary: They dump water believing they are near

acts.name: rescue
acts.summary: Guide digs deep and finds water

title: The Prince and the Painted Jackal
summary: A prince sees through a jackal painted as a divine beast by making it howl.
moral: True identity always shows through disguise

acts.name: test
acts.summary: Prince makes animal sounds at night

acts.name: exposure
acts.summary: Jackal howls back revealing its nature

title: The Lion's Skin
summary: A donkey wearing a lion's skin terrifies everyone until its bray gives it away.
moral: A fool cannot hide behind a wise disguise forever

acts.name: disguise
acts.summary: Donkey finds and wears lion skin

title: The Dove's Gratitude
summary: A dove is saved by an ant; later the dove drops a twig that trips a hunter about to shoot the ant.
moral: Kindness always comes back to you

title: The Fish and the Drought
summary: A fish leads his school to dig a channel to a larger lake before their pond dries up.
moral: A wise leader acts before crisis strikes

title: The Peacock and the Snake
summary: A peacock protects a village by eating snakes; villagers ungratefully cage it.
moral: Ingratitude is the blight of humanity

acts.name: greed
acts.summary: Villagers cage peacock for its feathers

title: The Greedy Merchant
summary: A merchant refuses a fair trade for a golden bowl, loses it when a second merchant recognizes its value.
moral: Greed causes you to lose fair opportunities

acts.name: chance
acts.summary: Woman offers old bowl for trade

acts.name: loss
acts.summary: Honest merchant buys it fairly instead

title: The Sparrow and the Elephant
summary: A tiny sparrow recruits friends to take revenge on an elephant that crushed her eggs.
moral: Unity of the small can defeat the great

acts.name: alliance
acts.summary: Sparrow recruits fly, frog, and crow

acts.name: victory
acts.summary: Elephant falls into pit through teamwork

title: The Monkey Bridge
summary: A monkey king stretches his body across a river chasm to let his troop cross safely.
moral: The greatest leaders serve their people with their very lives

acts.name: bridge
acts.summary: Monkey king becomes a living bridge

acts.name: honor

title: The Tiger and the Traveler
summary: A tiger offers a golden bracelet as bait; a traveler's greed leads him into the trap.
moral: Temptation is the hunter's most effective trap

acts.name: greed
acts.summary: Traveler wades through mud toward it

title: The Woodpecker and the Lion
summary: A woodpecker removes a bone from a lion's throat; the lion refuses to repay the favor.
moral: Do not expect gratitude from the ungrateful

acts.name: help
acts.summary: Woodpecker removes bone from lion's throat

title: The Hawk and the Nightingale
summary: A hawk catches a nightingale who argues she is too small to eat; the hawk keeps her anyway.
moral: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush

acts.name: argument
acts.summary: Nightingale argues she is too small

title: The Turtle King
summary: A turtle king refuses to leave his beloved lake despite drought warnings and is captured.
moral: Attachment to comfort can cost you your freedom
